children: European stocks were subdued on Tuesday, with both the STOXX 50 and STOXX 600 hovering around the flatline after gaining nearly 1% in the previous session.
The technology rally seen in the US overnight failed to carry over into European markets, while oil prices edged higher following a four-session losing streak.
Investors continued to monitor developments on the diplomatic front, particularly efforts to end the conflict with Iran.
US President Trump is due to address the United Nations General Assembly later today and has left open the possibility of meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian.
Among the largest companies, ASML (-0.2%), HSBC (-0.8%), Banco Santander (-0.6%) and Allianz (-2.9%) traded lower, while Shell (+0.8%) and TotalEnergies (+1%) moved higher.
The software sector was firmer, led by Prosus (+3.7%), while automakers and pharmaceutical stocks were under pressure.

title: European Stocks Cautious
